canonical_title: The Book of Philip K. Dick
summary: Canonical record for The Book of Philip K. Dick, PKD's short-story collection. Linked to a single archive manifestation preserved in the archive.
page_summary:
The Book of Philip K. Dick is the canonical works-table record for PKD's short-story collection corpus item. The record links the archive's preserved manifestation of the work to the broader corpus and gives researchers a single place to follow its bibliographic and interpretive context.

The preserved archive item here is The Book of Philip K. Dick (1973) (1973).

The source record itself summarizes the work as follows: The Book of Philip K. Dick is a 1973 short story collection dedicated to Leslie Busby. The volume collects stories written primarily between 1952 and 1955: Nanny, The Turning Wheel, The Defenders, Adjustment Team, PSI-Man, The Commuter, A Present for Pat, Breakfast at Twilight, and Shell Game.

The text excerpt includes the opening of "Nanny," which begins with Mary Fields reflecting on how the Nanny robot has transformed her household. The story establishes a characteristically Dickian domestic setting where advanced technology has been seamlessly integrated into suburban family life.

These early stories demonstrate the themes that would define Dick's entire career: the intersection of technology and everyday domestic life, questions about automation and human dependency, and the uncanny quality of apparently benign suburban existence. "Adjustment Team" was later adapted as the 2011 film The Adjustment Bureau, and "The Commuter" was adapted for the Electric Dreams television series. The collection captures Dick at the beginning of his career, writing prolifically for the SF magazine market while developing the distinctive voice and concerns that would later produce his greatest novels.

The entry is most useful when tracing publication context, later commentary, or relationships to other works.
